decision: Rohan ruled (for Kyaloon): lab results enter the evaluation, and being tested is never a score bonus by itself.
why: A test report is evidence about the product. The act of testing is not a property that earns points.
result: Carried into the harness as an example stage rule of create_pack. The Kyaloon v3 pack prompt still gives +1 (docs/research/2026-10-24-kyaloon-patterns.md).

decision: Rohan ruled (for Kyaloon): the evaluation writes typed facts against field keys, and the attributes table owns the names.
why: One vocabulary for the evaluation, the layout and the answer engine.
evidence: Kyaloon RealDose decisions trail of the answer engine
result: Carried. In the harness, attributes belong to nodes and outputs name attributes of their node only.

decision: Rohan ruled: criteria rest on node attributes. A measurable attribute is a number, or a flag with details. A rating is a rational judgement on measurable things.
why: Most things are measurable and definable in some shape or form. That is what rating should generally be if it is an automated grading system.

decision: Rohan ruled: social cues stay out of grading.
why: Public sentiment can often swing emotionally.

decision: Rohan ruled: an attribute value is a number, a word, a list of words, or a flag. Each attribute carries a reference to why it was made, which connects it to the records and facts system, the packs and the rubrics.
why: One value model for each attribute, and provenance that traces each attribute to what needs it.

decision: Rohan stated the problem: today the AI decides what rules make up an evaluation of a product, from meta instructions that nobody can enforce.
why: today the ai decides what rules constitutes an evaluation of a product based on some meta instruction which are not really enforceable.

decision: Rohan ruled: rules form a graph, not a linear book. Graph nodes are projections of the category nodes. Each rule has the domains and fields where it applies.
why: A rule applies where its category applies.

decision: Rohan ruled: rules and instructions are the same thing for now.
why: One concept to enforce.
evidence: For now we dont make any distinction between instructions and rules. rules = instructions.

decision: Rohan ruled the node levels: a top node creates the criteria and the rules for defining evaluations; the next nodes create attributes, research records and the reasons for each attribute; leaf nodes get evaluation packs that filter the criteria and attributes and create a scoring system; the record system holds the research behind the rules.
why: Each level owns what it creates.

decision: Rohan ruled: a stage researches with two kinds of tools, internet research and retrieval of past relevant work (criteria tables and research records). A ruleset judge then checks that the rules hold.
why: The research must reuse past work and stay checkable.

decision: Rohan ruled: the rules also define the outputs of each stage, and the judge checks the outputs against them. The graph assimilates an output after the ruleset checkers approve it.
why: Every output has a defined shape and a check.

decision: Rohan ruled: attributes mean things that relate to products only.
why: we are constraining the attributes to actually mean things that relate to products.

decision: Rohan ruled: node creation is a stage. Criteria pass down from the parent. The stage researches what each criterion means at the child, how relevant it is, and which additions it needs (like the extra points of the Kyaloon v3 packs). Rulesets govern pack creation and layout creation.
why: The graph lets the model traverse the stages.

decision: Rohan ruled: build an evaluation harness on Mastra, use google-research/harness2 for the ideas of recursive self-improvement, and open-source it in a new public repo.
why: lets create an evaluation harness and "we will open source this shit."

decision: Claude decided for Rohan: only a domain node creates criteria. A lower node judges relevance and meaning and adds additions. A concern that no criterion covers becomes an addition or a proposed change at the domain node.
why: Products of one domain stay comparable on one set of criteria. Kyaloon v3 has the same rule (a concern that fits no criterion goes into the adjustment guidance).

decision: Claude decided for Rohan: a child node can add rules but cannot remove or weaken an inherited rule. A change to an inherited rule is a new version at the node that owns it.
why: One owner for each rule, so two nodes never hold two versions of one rule.
evidence: Prior art: deny wins in Claude Code permission rules (docs/research/2026-10-24-rule-enforcement-prior-art.md)

decision: Claude decided for Rohan: an operator names each new node. A stage that proposes new nodes is future work.
why: Smallest first step. Node proposal needs its own rules.
result: graph.walkthrough, graph.not_decided. Rohan can reverse it.

decision: Claude decided for Rohan: the graph accepts an output when each strict rule passes. A person decides when the repair budget is spent or a strict rule gives cannot verify. A person still gates each pack before it grades a product.
why: Rohan said that the graph assimilates what the ruleset checkers approve. The pack gate of Kyaloon v3 stays, because a pack grades real products.

decision: Claude decided for Rohan: stage rules live as files in git, reviewed by PR. Derived rules live in the graph store with versions and provenance.

result: enforce.choices. Rohan had this choice open since 2026-10-23.

decision: Claude decided for Rohan: each judge call answers one rule. One call can judge many items of the same rule.
why: Many rules in one prompt lower judge accuracy.
result: enforce.deciders. Rohan had this choice open since 2026-10-23.

decision: Claude decided for Rohan: an attribute value that fails its shape rule stays as raw text with the result cannot verify. It never becomes a typed value.
why: A silent drop is a silent reject, and a guessed type is a silent accept.
